statement: A finite complete-intersection Fano problem of degree strictly less than 75,000 has full symmetric Galois group unless its type is (r,n,d•)=(1,3,(3)) or (r,2r+2,(2,2)) with r≥1.

answer.text: A finite complete-intersection Fano problem of degree strictly less than 75,000 has full symmetric Galois group unless its type is (r,n,d•)=(1,3,(3)) or (r,2r+2,(2,2)) with r≥1. Twelve previously undetermined types are proved fully symmetric by exact verification of a double root and interval certification of every remaining simple solution.

notes:
The theorem is rigorous, combining symbolic computation and interval certification. The threshold is strict. The excluded cubic-surface and two-quadric families have Weyl groups and are not asserted symmetric.

A finite complete-intersection Fano problem of degree strictly less than 75,000 has full symmetric Galois group unless its type is (r,n,d•)=(1,3,(3)) or (r,2r+2,(2,2)) with r≥1. Twelve previously undetermined types are proved fully symmetric by exact verification of a double root and interval certification of every remaining simple solution.
scope: r-dimensional projective linear spaces on a general complex complete intersection of the specified multidegree in P^n, when the Fano scheme is finite.
